LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS (PRONUNCIATION, ARTICULATION)

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and Speaking Listening for gist Imitative Speaking Phonological awaren
Topic 1.1: Phonological awareness (pronunciation, articulation)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Phonological awareness (pronunciation, articulation), part of Listening and Speaking Listening for gist Imitative Speaking Phonological awaren in Grade 5 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: Why is correct pronunciation important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to basic greetings and different ways of saying one's name (z. B Guten Tag! ich heiße..., Hallo! ich bin..., Guten Morgen, mein Name ist.) from a variety of sources, e.g. the teacher, recorded audio/video,

2. listen to different ways of asking for one's name and their responses (z. B wie heißt du? ich heiße... wer bist du? ich bin.. wie ist dein Name? Mein Name ist...),

3. ask and respond to questions on various ways of saying own name with peers (wie ist dein Familienname, Vorname, Nachname, Spitzname),

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to basic greetings and different ways of saying one's name (z. B Guten Tag! ich heiße..., Hallo! ich bin..., Guten Morgen, mein Name ist.) from a variety of sources, e.g. the teacher, recorded audio/video,
2. listen to different ways of asking for one's name and their responses (z. B wie heißt du? ich heiße... wer bist du? ich bin.. wie ist dein Name? Mein Name ist...),
3. ask and respond to questions on various ways of saying own name with peers (wie ist dein Familienname, Vorname, Nachname, Spitzname),

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Phonological awareness (pronunciation, articulation) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: The learner is guided to: work in teams with peers as peers role play and record audios / videos on basic greetings and

share in plenum.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social Cohesion: The learner develops an awareness and respect of other people as they greet and say their names.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner links the concept of greetings and introducing oneself to the same concept in English and Kiswahili.
